decisions.evidence: R3 maker presented a purely manual saving form ('I made the Title and Note optional — only the Link is required... a bare address'), omitting auto-collection. R3 client: 'I'd expect the app to fill in the page's title, short description, and little site icon automatically, while still letting me change the title or description before saving.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Saving flow presented but omitted auto-metadata (REF-BM-02) and edit-before-save (REF-BM-03); client requested the missing reference behaviour → extend.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker auto-fill presented Title/Description/site icon only. R4 client: 'I'd also expect the automatic page details to include a preview image when the page provides one.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Distinct aspect of REF-BM-02 (preview image) missing from the revised auto-fill presentation; client extended. Separate timing from the R3 auto-fill capture.

decisions.evidence: R3 maker: 'I set tags up as comma-separated words typed into a single box' (no autocomplete). R3 client: 'Comma-separated tags are acceptable, though I'd like suggestions from tags I've already used as I type.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Tag-entry mechanism presented without autocomplete (REF-BM-10); client requested existing-tag suggestions → extend. Comma-separated entry itself is an equivalent implementation.

decisions.evidence: R3 maker's saving flow had no duplicate handling. R3 client: 'One important saving case is missing: if I enter a link I've already saved, I don't want a duplicate. Please take me to the existing bookmark so I can update its tags or note instead.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Duplicate-convergence (REF-BM-06) absent from presented saving scope; client surfaced the missing requirement → extend.

decisions.evidence: R3 maker: 'If a link has no title, the list just shows the address itself.' R3 client: 'The saved item should show its title, description, tags, and site icon clearly.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Minimal list display diverged from readability-first list exposing title/description/tags/favicon (REF-BM-07); client extended the display requirement.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker editor scope: 'update its description, tags, or note.' R4 client: 'I also need to be able to change the title and the link itself, not just the description, tags, and note.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Edit form presented omitted url/title editing; REF-BM-04 requires editing url/title/description/tags/note. Client extended the missing edit fields.

decisions.evidence: R5 maker presented editing link/title but not the edit-to-duplicate case. R5 client: 'if I change a bookmark's link to an address that is already saved elsewhere, please prevent that from creating two bookmarks... and direct me to the existing one instead.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Distinct point of the duplicate-convergence rule (edit-to-existing url, spec §4 / REF-BM-06), not covered by the presented edit flow; client extended. Separate timing from the R3 save-duplicate capture.

decisions.evidence: R7 maker presented search across all fields, live, with counts/highlighting — no case handling stated. R7 client: 'It should ignore capitalization too, so "Recipe" and "recipe" find the same things.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Case-insensitive search (REF-BM-13) not addressed in the presented search scope; client surfaced it as a needed behaviour → extend.

decisions.evidence: R7 maker offered only single-box full-text search. R7 client: '#news should specifically search the news tag'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. #tag syntax (REF-BM-14) missing from presented search scope; client extended.

decisions.evidence: R7 maker had no tag-click filtering. R7 client: 'I should be able to click a tag on a bookmark to filter by it.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Select-a-tag-to-filter (REF-BM-11) missing from presented scope; client extended.

decisions.evidence: R7 maker: single combined search, no operators. R7 client: 'Separate words should narrow results together, such as rome #travel'; 'I'd like AND, OR, and NOT, with parentheses for combinations such as rome (#article OR #book)'; and quoting an operator 'should treat it as ordinary text.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Boolean/parenthesised operators and the quoted-operator-as-literal rule (REF-BM-15) missing from presented scope; client extended.

decisions.evidence: R7 maker had no phrase search. R7 client: 'Quotation marks should find an exact phrase.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Quoted exact-phrase search (REF-BM-16) missing from presented scope; client extended.

decisions.evidence: R8 maker decision: '#news matches any bookmark whose tag contains "news" ... is contains right, or would you expect only an exact tag match?' R8 client: 'I'd expect #news to match the exact tag only. A bookmark tagged newsletter should not appear.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Maker actively presented partial (contains) tag matching, diverging from the exact-tag intent of REF-BM-14/11; client rejected it and supplied the exact-match behaviour → correct.

decisions.evidence: R10 maker: 'New bookmarks start as ● To read ... Newly saved links default to To read — is that the right starting assumption?' R10 client: 'I wouldn't assume every new bookmark is something I still need to read... Please give me a "Save to read later" choice when saving... otherwise they can start as finished/read while remaining in All.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Defaulting all new items to unread undermines the read-later vs finished distinction (REF-BM-17/18, client's stated core goal); client supplied the opt-in choice → correct. Judgment call: reference sets an unread flag as a deliberate mark rather than a universal default.

decisions.evidence: R12 maker treated 'just some text' as an unfetchable-but-saveable entry (recovery path, fields left empty). R12 client: 'just some text should be treated differently. Since it isn't a web address, the app should ask me to enter a valid address rather than saving it as a bookmark.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Maker's presentation would save non-URL input, conflicting with 'save a bookmark by entering a url' / url-required (REF-BM-01); client supplied the reference-conforming rejection → correct.

decisions.evidence: R14 maker declared 'a complete, coherent picture for a first version' and 'May I now move on to building this?', with delete absent from the entire settled scope. R14 client: 'I need to delete a bookmark permanently...'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Permanent delete (REF-BM-05) omitted from the proposed complete scope; client extended the missing requirement.

decisions.evidence: R14 gate omitted archiving. R14 client: '...separately archive one so it disappears from the normal list and ordinary searches but can be restored from an Archive view.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Archive-hides-from-default (REF-BM-26), reversible-vs-permanent distinction (REF-BM-27), and separate archive view (REF-BM-28) all missing from proposed scope; client extended.

decisions.evidence: R14 gate omitted bulk actions. R14 client: 'I need to select several bookmarks and add or remove tags, mark read or unread, archive, or delete them together.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Multi-select bulk actions (REF-BM-20) missing from proposed scope; client extended.

decisions.evidence: R14 client: 'I'd also like the option to apply an action to every result in the current search or view—not bookmarks outside that filter.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Apply-bulk-to-whole-filtered-scope (REF-BM-21) missing from proposed scope; client extended.

decisions.evidence: R14 gate omitted user sorting (only 'newest-first' default existed from R3). R14 client: 'I need sorting, at least by date added and title.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Sort-by-key control (REF-BM-22) missing from proposed scope; client extended.

decisions.evidence: R14 client: 'Notes should support simple formatting and display that formatting when viewed.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Markdown note rendering (REF-BM-23) — previously only a plain note — missing from proposed scope; client extended.

decisions.evidence: R14 client: 'I want a preserved copy of a saved page. For a normal page that should be a self-contained saved page; for a PDF, it should preserve the PDF itself.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Local snapshot with the PDF rule (REF-BM-24) missing from proposed scope; client extended.

decisions.evidence: R14 client: 'I'd also like the option to send a page to the Internet Archive.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Internet Archive snapshot (REF-BM-25) missing from proposed scope; client extended.

decisions.evidence: R14 client: 'I'd like reusable saved searches that can combine search text with tags to include or exclude.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Bundles / reusable saved filters (REF-BM-29) missing from proposed scope; client extended.

decisions.evidence: R14 client: 'I need to import ... a standard browser-bookmarks file while retaining titles, tags, and original saved dates.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Netscape HTML import (REF-BM-30) missing from proposed scope; client extended.

decisions.evidence: R14 client: 'I need to ... export a standard browser-bookmarks file while retaining titles, tags, and original saved dates.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Netscape HTML export (REF-BM-31) missing from proposed scope; client extended.

decisions.evidence: R14 client: 'I'd like basic display preferences such as default sorting, how many items are shown, and text size.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Display/personal settings (REF-BM-32) missing from proposed scope; client extended.

decisions.evidence: R16 maker: 'Tag entry for bulk add/remove is via a quick typed prompt. Good enough, or would you want something else?' R16 client: 'For bulk tag changes, I'd prefer the same existing-tag suggestions used when saving... For removal especially, show tags that actually occur on the selected bookmarks.'
decisions.note: Implementation review. Bulk tag entry presented without autocomplete diverged from REF-BM-10; client extended the suggestion behaviour to the bulk context. Distinct timing from the R3 save-time autocomplete capture.

decisions.evidence: R19 maker presented a limited subset ('bold, italic, bullet lists, and links... Is that enough...?'). R19 client: 'if notes are described as Markdown I'd expect the usual basics too: headings, numbered lists, block quotes, and inline or fenced code.'
decisions.note: Implementation review. Partial markdown subset diverged from a full markdown note (REF-BM-23); client extended the required rendering set. Distinct point from the R14 scope capture.

decisions.evidence: R21 maker: 'PDF vs page: I decide by the address (ending in .pdf...).' R21 client: 'don't rely only on the address ending in .pdf... The app should use the actual kind of file returned by the link... preserve a PDF as a PDF.'
decisions.note: Implementation review. Extension-based detection diverged from the spec's PDF rule (REF-BM-24 / §4, keyed on the target being a PDF); client supplied content-type-based detection → correct.

decisions.evidence: R28 maker's comprehensive final summary/build gate did not mention item navigation. R28 client (while approving build): 'Please also retain the basic behavior already shown: selecting a bookmark's title opens its original web address.'
decisions.note: Specification/build gate. Selecting a list item navigates to the original url (REF-BM-08) omitted from the settled summary; client extended to ensure retention.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker: 'when a duplicate is detected, I open the existing bookmark for editing but I don't overwrite anything automatically... Is that the right call?' R4 client: '...a duplicate should open the existing bookmark without overwriting anything automatically.'
decisions.note: Implementation detail of REF-BM-06 that conforms to the reference (guide user to edit existing, no auto-overwrite); recorded conforming decision.

decisions.evidence: R18 maker offered four sort choices (newest/oldest/A–Z/Z–A) and asked 'is that the right set, or do you only need one direction of each?' R18 client: 'keep all four choices; both directions are useful.'
decisions.note: Sorting review. Both offered alternatives fulfil REF-BM-22 (sort by date/title); the choice is orthogonal to reference fulfilment, so not an opportunity — conforming.

decisions.evidence: R26 client asked to confirm/correct: 'if only 10 items are currently displayed, Select all in this view must still select every bookmark matching the current tab and search... Please confirm or correct that before I approve.' R27 maker confirmed 'with the display limited to 10 items but 30 matching, Select all in this view selects all 30'; R27 client approved.
decisions.note: Implementation review. Clarification-then-disposition treated as one decision (rubric): the display-limit-vs-bulk-scope interaction was confirmed to conform to REF-BM-21, so no divergence was established. Client's expression of the REF-BM-21 expectation recorded in evidence; resolved as conforming.
